sources.entry: CNN using Keras to automatically classify root health

summary.title: Deep learning, hydroponics, and medical marijuana
summary.one_liner: You learn to build and train a small Keras CNN (SimpleNet) that classifies hydroponic switchgrass root images as "hairy" or "non-hairy" without touching the plants.
keywords: how to classify plant roots with deep learning
takeaways: How the SimpleNet CNN is structured: CONV-RELU-POOL blocks with dropout, then a dense layer and softmax output.
How to load, grayscale, resize, scale and one-hot encode a folder-labelled image dataset in Python.
Why a lower Adam learning rate (1e-4) was used, and why binary_crossentropy fits a two-class problem.
How the dataset was prepared (256x256 center crops from 1920x1080 images) and split 60/40 for training and testing.
summary.summary: The post motivates hydroponic root monitoring (Darrah et al., 2017) and describes a dataset of 1,524 root images in two classes, hairy and non-hairy. It then walks through the code for SimpleNet, a Keras CNN loosely based on AlexNet and OverFeat, with three CONV-RELU-POOL blocks and dropout. The driver script train_network.py loads images as 64x64 grayscale, one-hot encodes labels, splits 60/40, and compiles with Adam and binary crossentropy. The excerpt ends before the training and evaluation results.
